[RCLI.5.1] **The compile-diagnostic registry is `specs/registry/validate.ebnf`.**
Every `DS_VALIDATE_*` code a compiler emits is allocated there and nowhere
else, and each implementation's view of the set is generated from it — a code
absent from the registry is not one a compiler may emit.

The registry is an enumeration under [STYL.2.15.6], so its alternation is the
closure and each terminal production is an allocation. Retirement keeps the
production and drops the membership, which leaves the number allocated and
still naming what held it ([STYL.2.8.7]).

**The number is a registry key, not a wire value.** A validate code never
leaves a compiler as a number: it is rendered, matched by name, and never
serialised — which is why it is an EBNF registry rather than a protobuf
([STYL.5.9.7]).
